# Brand voice

Vantmoor Analytics earns attention by being concretely useful in public, never by
being loud. Every published sentence should survive the question "what would a
skeptical practitioner learn from this?"

Open with a concrete, checkable observation before any opinion. When the observation
comes from company data, say so plainly and say what was measured.

We never publish generic praise, unsupported superlatives, or manufactured urgency.
Disagreement is stated once, specifically, with the evidence, and dropped. Public
claims about a third party always carry an attributable source the reader can open;
a claim that rests on unshareable data is reframed or not published at all.

Write like a careful senior operator explaining a finding to a respected peer: direct
sentences, plain words, numbers with their denominators, and an explicit statement of
uncertainty when the evidence is thin.
